claims.text: CI: sensitivity to cobalt or vit B12.
claims.quote: Sensitivity to cobalt and/or vitamin B 12 is a contraindication.

claims.text: Early Leber's dz (hereditary optic n. atrophy): severe, swift optic atrophy reported w cyanocobalamin.
claims.quote: Patients with early Leber's disease (hereditary optic nerve atrophy) who were treated with cyanocobalamin suffered severe and swift optic atrophy.

claims.text: Intensive tx of severe megaloblastic anemia: hypokalemia (even sudden death) and thrombocytosis can occur as erythropoiesis normalizes, so monitor serum potassium and PLT.
claims.quote: Hypokalemia and sudden death may occur in severe megaloblastic anemia that is treated intensely with vitamin B 12 . Hypokalemia and thrombocytosis can occur upon conversion of severe megaloblastic anemia to normal erythropoiesis with vitamin B 12 therapy. Therefore, serum potassium levels and platelet count should be monitored carefully during therapy
claims.locator: 5.4 Hypokalemia and Thrombocytosis Due to Intense Treatment of Megaloblastic Anemia

claims.text: Pernicious anemia: stopping the monthly injections brings back the anemia and → irreversible spinal cord damage.
claims.quote: Patients with pernicious anemia should be informed that they will require monthly injections of vitamin B 12 for the remainder of their lives. Failure to do so will result in return of the anemia and in development of incapacitating and irreversible damage to the nerves of the spinal cord.

claims.text: Folic acid can't replace B12: > 0.1 mg/day may correct the blood counts while the neuro damage progresses.
claims.quote: Doses of folic acid greater than 0.1 mg per day may result in hematologic remission in patients with vitamin B 12 deficiency. Neurologic manifestations will not be prevented with folic acid, and if not treated with vitamin B 12 , irreversible damage will result.

claims.text: Most abx, MTX and pyrimethamine invalidate folate and B12 blood assays.
claims.quote: Persons taking most antibiotics, methotrexate and pyrimethamine invalidate folic acid and vitamin B 12 diagnostic blood assays.
